processing: No account specific to this line is documented; Phoenix dancong is generally sun-withered, shaken and rested in rounds, then fixed, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: Not documented for this line; spring is the main picking for Phoenix dancong in general.
appearance_dry: Not specifically described; dancong in general is long, twisted and dark brown.
appearance_liquor: Not specifically described; dancong liquor is usually clear golden to light amber.
appearance_wet: Not specifically described; dancong leaves usually show reddened edges after shaking.
taste_profile: The name itself points to a bitter taste, but no reliable tasting description of this line is documented. Dancong lines in general carry a returning sweetness.

brewing.notes: General dancong approach, with slightly less leaf as a cautious start for a tea named for bitterness. Adjust to taste.

vintage_note: No selling pattern is documented for this line. What is usual for Phoenix dancong is sale by spring harvest of the current year, sometimes with older roasted stock marked by year. Expect it rarely, if at all, under this exact name.
description:
Ku Wei Cha, literally 'bitter-taste tea', is one of the many named lines of Phoenix Mountain dancong. It is listed outside the ten main aroma types, alongside pomelo-flower, orange-flower and fuzi-scented lines.

That listing is nearly all that is on record. A Chinese tea science overview files it among lines named for their quality, by aroma and by taste, so the bitterness in the name seems to be the identifying trait rather than a fault.

How it tastes in practice is not well described. As a starting point, treat it as you would other dancong, and use less leaf and quick pours until you know how much bitterness it carries.

A vendor's list of Phoenix trees has a group called ku zhong, bitter-leaf bushes, mostly in Wudong Village. Whether that is the same thing as Ku Wei Cha is not established, so ask a seller what they mean by the name.
history: Little is documented. The name turns up in Chinese lists of Phoenix dancong lines and in the classification of them by aroma and taste, with no date, place of selection or person attached.
